grade_reason: The only AI remark found in her own words is from a July 2025 hearing on AI and crime, about policing and privacy, which is level D; no 2026 statement about AI and no statement about catastrophic AI risk was found.
notes: All seven web searches ran in this second attempt (official-site search, superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, pause or moratorium, China agreement or treaty, 'AI safety', and the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act); none returned any statement by McBath on catastrophic AI risk, superintelligence, a pause, or China talks. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, Sanders and Casar): no source found names McBath as a cosponsor. Coverage names Ocasio-Cortez and says nine other House Democrats cosponsored without naming them (Forkast article, opened); the Congress.gov cosponsor page returned HTTP 403 and could not be opened, so cosponsorship is not fully ruled out. From the first attempt: the official site home page and press release listing pages 1 and 2 (16 June to 27 October 2026) show no AI-related releases; the 26 August 2026 job training release does not mention AI. Press release pages 3 onward were not checked. The statement date is the article date on the repost (16 July 2025); the hearing is assumed to be the same day but this was not confirmed. Partial quote left out: the article quotes her saying lawmakers must determine "what those guardrails should look like and put them in place" (a fragment inside a paraphrase, so not used as a quote). Paraphrases left out: she cautioned that police use of AI could violate the privacy of law-abiding people and proposed privacy safeguards for AI tools used by police. A 2022 release welcoming a $65 million AI manufacturing grant to a Georgia Tech-led coalition is before 2025 and was not used. Many-signer House letters of August and September 2026 were not searched, per instructions.
